meta.title: La Bachillera · History, planning and current problems
meta.description: Informational site for the La Bachillera neighbourhood (Seville): history, AGI-02 urban planning, a document archive and a map of the electrical infrastructure.

hero.title: La Bachillera
hero.subtitle: The history, the urban planning and the problems the neighbourhood still faces: from the 77 years it took residents to register their homes to the power lines that still run over their houses.

history.title: 77 years: from self-built homes to a deed
history.lede: The neighbourhood began as self-built housing, with no deeds and no urban plan. These eight milestones sum up how, eight decades on, its residents finally got to register their homes.

items.text: The Asociación Sevillana de Caridad inherits the land. It leases plots to smallholder herders, who pass them on to other families with its permission: the start of self-built housing with no property deeds.
The neighbourhood grows through self-building, with no urban plan and no public facilities. The land remains a single registered plot and homes are never formally deeded.
Residents set up the Comisión de Barrio (neighbourhood commission) and produce a participatory planning assessment, alongside the drafting of the new PGOU.
The PGOU designates the neighbourhood as Integrated Management Area AGI-02: it reverses a planned eviction and defers detailed planning to a future special plan.
The PERI is approved on an initial basis, but around 300 resident objections stall the case for years.
Seville's City Council gives final, unanimous approval to the PERI, after 8 years in process.
The parcelling deed splitting the original single plot is signed before a notary.
Re-parcelling is completed: 202 independent plots. Residents can finally register their homes, 77 years on.

planning.title: AGI-02 and the special plan (PERI)
planning.lede: Seville's General Urban Plan (PGOU) designated the neighbourhood as Integrated Management Area AGI-02 and deferred its detailed planning to a Special Urban Renewal Plan (PERI). The PERI doesn't amend the General Plan: it's the development plan that carries it out for this specific area.
enabledItems: Regularising ownership: splitting the single plot into 202 independent parcels.
Defining the neighbourhood's streets and open public space.
pendingItems: The action programme against substandard housing.

electric.title: The power line problem
electric.lede: Three high-voltage lines cross the El Manchón area directly above homes; two medium-voltage lines run through the centre of the neighbourhood, with poles along Calle Tilo. The Empalme substation, in San Jerónimo, is the key constraint on any fix.
electric.paragraph1: Undergrounding or rerouting the lines is still pending, and depends on Endesa and Red Eléctrica de España. In 2017, the City Council, Red Eléctrica and Endesa signed a €55M agreement for a similar project in the Distrito Este: the precedent cited for La Bachillera. In 2022, municipal groups raised the issue in the Control Commission and in full Council session, in February and April, asking for a timeline.
electric.paragraph2: In July 2026, the Gerencia de Urbanismo began processing a targeted amendment to the PGOU that keeps the Empalme substation at its current site, while proposing to reroute and bury the lines running over the neighbourhood's homes.
